description.narrative: Madi Okollo and Arua districts, Uganda
Targeted refugees (12,583 people) and host communities (6427 people).

This project adopts a PGI-sensitive approach towards WASH, watershed management and disaster risk reduction, using both resilience frameworks and data support as tools to strengthen community resilience to water-related risks.

To provide lifesaving services to a total of 12,583 people in Rhino settlement, Madi Okollo District and 6,427 host community members in KamKam village in Arua District, including children, girls, boys, women, elderly and persons with disabilities, for a period of 2 years. The proposed strategy will focus on the integrated Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Promotion (WASH), Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Disaster Preparedness and Water Catchment/environmental conservation activities to increase community resilience against water-related risks.
To reduce the impact of floods, droughts, and environmental degradation (mainly deforestation) and epidemics including the COVID-19 pandemic.
